general_information.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_information.Description: 1. Course Objectives: This course aims to provide learners with a comprehensive understanding of how technology is applied within modern banking systems. Students will explore the historical development of banking technology, key digital infrastructures, and core banking functions such as payments and customer interaction. The course also examines opportunities and risks arising from digital transformation in the financial sector. By the end of the course, learners will be able to analyze banking technology ecosystems and engage effectively with both technical and business stakeholders in the industry. 2. Course Content: The course is organised in six blocks. (1) Foundations of digital banking, including the evolution of banking and its technology landscape; (2) Architecture and data, covering core banking systems, databases, and integration technologies; (3) Digital channels, such as internet/mobile banking and customer interaction across platforms; (4) Payments and operations, including card payments, interbank systems, and risk management technologies; (5) Regulation and governance, focusing on compliance, data protection, and technology management; and (6) Future trends in digital banking, supported by an applied project. 3. Activities and Teaching Methodology: Of the 60 sessions, roughly 40 are guided lectures and case discussions and the remainder are applied workshops, project checkpoints, assessment and review. Workshops ask students to trace transactions end-to-end, read a public banking API portal, audit a real bank's cross-channel journey, map an instant payment flow, and translate a regulatory requirement into technology requirements. All technical content is delivered at conceptual and interpretive level: students read, explain and evaluate architectures and process flows; no programming, configuration or systems administration is required.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, workshops, assignments and case studies given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Read the assigned textbook sections before each session; sections marked as background reading are self-study and are not assessed in depth - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information
general_information.Tools: - FPT University learning material system: https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ - Personal Laptop - Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) - A free diagramming tool (draw.io, Lucidchart or equivalent) for architecture and journey-mapping workshops - Publicly available bank/fintech and regulator materials (annual reports, developer/API portals, Open Banking and payment scheme documentation; SBV/NAPAS materials for the Vietnamese context)
general_information.Note: Introduction-level course (code 201, semester 3), no pre-requisite. Content is selected against the course objective rather than covering the textbook exhaustively. Every chapter is classified as Core (taught and assessed), Awareness (context only, lightly assessed) or Self-study (background reading, not assessed) - see the 'Textbook Coverage' sheet. Legacy and telecoms-engineering material (CORBA, CICS internals, SIP/H.323, dialler and workforce-scheduling mechanics) and UK-specific scheme timetables are treated as awareness or worked examples only.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Describe the role of technology in the banking and financial services business, including banking products and services in the digital era, the technology inheritance, digital-first banking models and the current banking-fintech landscape.

Explain how a bank works as a technology system, including the core banking platform, database and platform architecture, availability and resilience, single customer view, integration and banking APIs, microservices, and banking data and reporting.

Analyse digital banking channels and customer journeys - internet and mobile banking, authentication and digital onboarding, branch, ATM and contact centre - against consistency, availability, security and accessibility.

Analyse payment and banking-operations technologies, including card payments, clearing and settlement, interbank payment schemes, payment platform technology, credit operations and fraud detection, and interpret their operational, cost and risk implications.

Evaluate the regulatory, compliance and governance environment of banking technology - payment and data-protection regulation, Open Banking, KYC/AML obligations, operational resilience, the technology function and sourcing - and its impact on technology decisions.
Develop and present, individually and in teams, a feasible technology-enabled solution to a digital banking or fintech problem, evaluating risks, constraints and the responsible use of data.

assessments.Question Type: Group project with rubric criteria; report or slide deck, presentation and Q&A
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: End-to-end guided project for a selected bank, digital bank or fintech proposition: problem framing and business/technology context; channel and customer-experience design (Ch. 4); payment and banking-operations technology (Ch. 5-7); regulatory, compliance and resilience requirements (Ch. 8-9); a feasible technology-enabled solution with risks, constraints and recommendations.
assessments.Grading Guide: ASM content: end-to-end technology solution for a selected bank, digital bank or fintech proposition, covering problem framing, channel and customer-experience design, payment and operations technology, regulatory and resilience requirements, and a feasible solution with risks and recommendations. Grouping: groups of 4-5 students, formed in Session 30; each member owns a named section and is assessed on it. Grading: 100 points; a group mark is adjusted by individual contribution and Q&A performance. Presentation: report or slide deck plus a 15-minute group presentation and 10-minute Q&A; all technical terms and diagrams must be explained in business language. Location: prepared outside class; presented in class in Sessions 58-59. Parties involved: students, instructor and peer groups; a checkpoint is held in Session 54.
assessments.Note: Released in Session 30, checkpoint in Session 54, finalised in Session 57, presented in Sessions 58-59. Instruction and schedule must be presented in the Course Implementation Plan.

assessments.Question Type: Applied written assignment with rubric criteria; report with architecture and customer-journey diagrams
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Analysis of one approved bank/fintech and one selected digital service: business and technology context (Ch. 1-2); the core platform, integration, data and resilience delivering the service (Ch. 3); the digital channels and customer journey supporting it (Ch. 3 Sec. 3.10-3.11 and Ch. 4); risks and improvement recommendations. Expected level is business-technology interpretation, not technical implementation.
assessments.Grading Guide: ASM content: written analysis of one approved bank or fintech and one selected digital service, covering the business and technology context, the technology architecture delivering the service, the digital channels and customer journey, key risks and feasible recommendations. Grouping: individual work; no groups. Grading: 100 points; sources must be public and cited. Presentation: report of 2,000-2,500 words with at least one architecture diagram and one customer-journey diagram; submitted as a single file. Location: take-home; released Session 6, submitted Session 30. Parties involved: student and instructor; the instructor approves the chosen bank/fintech and marks the report.
assessments.Note: Released in Session 6 and submitted in Session 30. Instruction and schedule must be presented in the Course Implementation Plan.

assessments.Question Type: In-class discussion, exercises, case studies and practice-session outputs
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: All Core content of Chapters 1-10, with emphasis on applied interpretation: reading and explaining banking architecture diagrams, customer journeys, payment flows and regulatory requirements. No programming or system configuration is required.
assessments.Grading Guide: Participation scores will be given based on students' class attendance, preparation, quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussions, and building upon others’ comments.
assessments.Note: Recorded continuously across Sessions 1-60 and published to students at the end of the semester.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: Explain why a modern bank is a technology business, and compare an incumbent bank with a digital-first challenger on cost base, technology and customer proposition.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: Map a modern banking product or service to the technology and payment infrastructure needed to deliver it.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3
constructive_questions.Details: Explain what a bank inherits from decades of banking technology, and why legacy systems make digital change slow, costly and risky.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ4
constructive_questions.Details: Explain the roles of banks, challengers, payment schemes and processors in the current banking ecosystem.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ5
constructive_questions.Details: Draw a simple model of a bank and explain what the core banking platform must do to open an account, hold balances and process transactions.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ6
constructive_questions.Details: Explain what a banking database must guarantee for a transaction, and evaluate database architecture options for a banking system.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ7
constructive_questions.Details: Explain how a bank stays available to its customers and recovers from failure, and assess an outage against those measures.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8
constructive_questions.Details: Explain why a single customer view is difficult to achieve in a bank, and what business problems its absence creates.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ9
constructive_questions.Details: Explain why legacy transaction processing survives in banks and what constraints it places on a new digital proposition.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ10
constructive_questions.Details: Design a secure authentication and digital onboarding journey that balances customer friction, fraud risk and identity requirements.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ11
constructive_questions.Details: Evaluate what a banking or Open Banking API allows a third party to do, and what risks and controls it requires.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ12
constructive_questions.Details: Explain how a bank turns transaction data into management and regulatory reporting, and where big data adds value.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ13
constructive_questions.Details: Evaluate the role of branch and ATM technology in a digital-first bank, and decide what should be retained, automated or withdrawn.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ14
constructive_questions.Details: Design a cross-channel customer journey that remains consistent, available, secure and accessible across mobile, web and assisted channels.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ15
constructive_questions.Details: Trace a retail credit application through decisioning, and identify where automation adds most value and most risk.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ16
constructive_questions.Details: Explain how a bank uses technology to verify customers, screen against sanctions lists and detect money laundering, and assess the customer-friction trade-off.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ17
constructive_questions.Details: Trace a card payment from the terminal to the issuer, and explain the role, revenue and risk of each party in the four-party model.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ18
constructive_questions.Details: Compare batch, instant and high-value payment schemes, and explain how a payment instruction is created, addressed, screened and reconciled.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ19
constructive_questions.Details: Translate a regulatory requirement such as payment regulation, data protection or Open Banking into concrete technology and data obligations.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ20
constructive_questions.Details: Develop and defend a digital banking technology solution that connects the business problem, solution architecture, channels, payments, risks and regulation.
